messages.text: Trail parking lot looked glassy when I drove by. Want me to set up the basement timer instead?
Yes, please. I was up past midnight with parent emails and the essay stack, so I am not trusting my footing this morning.
Timer on the card table. Also the redbud has tiny bumps on the branches.
That almost makes up for the slush. Leave the curtain open so I can see it while I do my twenty minutes.
Clouds are breaking up. North lot after supper?
Yes, let's do the river side before it gets dark. I left my gray shoes by the garage door.
I'll grab both jackets. Same bench turnaround as Sunday?
That works. I like that we can get there in five minutes and still be home before the news.
Late meeting ran over. Could you grab Emma and Luke at 4:10?
Yes. I already set the blue round canister on the counter, so they will head there first.
Luke asked yesterday if the 'good lid' one was empty.
Not empty. I put the cracked pieces in a bag and moved them away from the kettle before I started picking at them.
For Sunday, do you want me to bring the lemon seltzers again? Dad said you still have most of that cabernet from Christmas.
Could you grab Emma at 5:15 if my meeting runs long? Luke has his folder in the front pocket.
Seltzers would be perfect. The bottle is almost decorative at this point.
Yes. I was already going to be near the school after I finish a quick call with Linda.
Emma needs one old family photo for school. Do you still have the box from the Sterling Heights basement?
Yes, the gray bin by Don's workbench. It has the Farmbrook house pictures and some from when you and Paul were little.
Also, please don't take more Advil before bed if your knee is cranky. Eat first and keep an eye on your cuff reading.
My 5:00 ran long. Could you grab Emma and Luke from the school lobby at 5:40?
Thanks. Also, Mark asked Don about the old papers from Grandma's file before he heads back toward Ohio.
Perfect. If you find one with all four of us, send it before bedtime?
Yes. I'll bring the booster cushion and keep them busy until your car pulls in.
I took one with lunch and that is plenty. Heating pad tonight.
I have the appointment cards and insurance copies in the blue binder. I'll pull them tonight after dinner.
I'll look after dinner. Don keeps saying the '85 envelope is in there too, so I may have to sort around his labels.
Thank you. Emma has the purple backpack and Luke has his library book due tomorrow.
Got it. I'll put macaroni on and text Paul back after they're settled.
That article I sent you is about boards getting shouted down again. Don't open the comments unless you want to ruin your night.
I skimmed it. It made me close the laptop and go back to Maria's chapter questions for tomorrow.
Maria is one of the newer people on your hall, right?
Yes. She and Ben are trying hard. I'd rather spend an hour on their book groups than sit through another downtown committee night.
Do you still want me to save you two seats at the Friday fish supper?
Let me skip this one. We had the plumber here yesterday, so I moved $400 over and Don and I are eating from the freezer this week.
Understood. I can bring choir folders Sunday so you don't have to make an extra trip.
That helps. I also put the fabric order back in the cart for April.
I can bring the lemon bars Sunday. Do you still need cups for choir coffee?
Yes please. I put you down for lemon bars, cups, and two packs of napkins. I have Edna for creamer and Mark for folding chairs.
You already have all of us sorted out.
Only because the list was getting squirrelly. I rewrote it after lunch and taped a copy inside my music folder.
Furnace guy quoted $640 for the inducer motor. Cheaper than the whole board.
Pay it out of the house envelope, not the March checking. I want that cushion to stay where it is.
Already figured. Thursday morning he comes.
Good. Once that's done I want to look at the spreadsheet again before I commit to anything for July.
Cousin Joanne posted that thing again about the new shot causing strokes in 40-somethings. She said her neighbor's coworker.
Oh Joanne. I pulled up the Michigan health page and the CDC page before I even finished my coffee. Nothing like what she's saying.
I'm going to ask Dr. Whitfield at my April visit too, just so I can tell Joanne I asked a real person.
Ha. Don't argue with her on Facebook, Ter. You'll be up till midnight.
Luke just found out they moved Friday's gym time to 6:15. Can you and Dad still get there?
Yes. We'll leave early and grab the bleacher seats near the scorer's table.
Thanks. Also Emma wants to know if she can wear the navy cap you bought downtown with the D on it.
Of course. Tell her Grandpa already put our March 29 TV time on the fridge, so she'll fit right in.
Would Sunday work for dinner? Emma asked if you were making the pot with the beans and carrots again.
Sunday works. I picked up celery and tomatoes at Kroger, so I can get that started after church.
Perfect. Luke will eat more if you leave the green bits small.
I’ll chop the basil and thyme fine. If the kids want bread with it, bring a loaf.
Did you see the photos I tagged you in on Facebook from Emma's spring concert? Luke is in the third row.
Saw them this afternoon, already saved two and shared one to my own page. Luke's bow tie is killing me.
Ha. I'll post the rest tonight. Aunt Linda already commented before I even finished uploading.
She lives on that app. I follow Emma's dance studio page too now so I can catch the recital reminders.
Did you see the school board piece in the Free Press? The funding formula stuff Emma's district is dealing with.
Saw it this morning. Honestly the way they're squeezing the teachers contract is what gets me. Megan's been saying the same thing about Emma's class sizes.
Yeah. And it lines up with what you were saying about that ballot measure on collective bargaining last fall.
It does. I keep landing on the same side when it's schools or the union question. Don rolls his eyes but he knows where I'm going to vote.
Found another box of Mom's stuff in the basement. Stack of those little Warren Woods Tower notepads she used to bring home from the front office, the ones with the bulldog at the top.
Oh my goodness. She wrote everything on those. Attendance call-ins, dentist appts, Dad's lunch shift swaps.
There's one from like 1979 with Dad's local number on it and 'tell him line 2 down again.' Lol. Want me to set them aside for you?
Yes please. Pull anything in her handwriting. I'll grab them next time I come out to Clinton Twp.
How'd parent conferences go? You were dreading the Wednesday block.
Long but good. Marcus's mom stayed after to talk. Her older boy Andre got pulled over on Van Dyke again Saturday night, third time since Christmas. He had his hands on the wheel the whole time.
Third time. Lord. He's the one in community college now?

Macomb, yeah. She said he's started taking a different route home. I just sat there. Don and I have driven that same stretch for forty years and I couldn't tell you the last time we got more than a wave from an officer.
Emma's spring concert moved to the 19th, Roberts Auditorium. You and Dad coming?
Wouldn't miss it. What time should we be there
6:30 doors. Also Emma wants to know what color you're wearing so she can match her ribbon lol
Tell her whatever sweater is clean that night. Probably the gray one. She can pick whichever ribbon she likes
Did the Classroom links finally open on the student Chromebooks, or is that still broken?
Opened for the older group after I changed the share setting. The younger ones still needed the paper packet because the quiz froze twice.
Send me a screenshot later if you want. Also please leave the building before the parking lot is empty.
Too late for that, but I am packing the notebook stacks now. I am at 46 hours counting Sunday planning.
Do we still need the Consumers envelope on the desk or did you already handle that one?
Handled it after coffee. I put the number in the March tab and stuck the paper on the fridge until it clears.
Good. I will stop moving your sticky notes then.
Please do. The yellow ones are mine, the blue one is for both of us.
Do you want me to bring back that folding table from Mark, or are you still using the dining room for papers?
Dining room is covered in the blue folder, Don's calculator, and the credit union printout. I told him we have to finish it before choir tomorrow.
You sounded wound up on the phone. Did you get outside before the rain?
Good. I can drop the table on the porch later so you two don't have to move cars around.
Pulled the dead stems by the garage and walked two blocks. Chest settled some once I stopped replaying that committee call.
That works. Nobody is here after lunch, so the porch is fine until Don brings it in.
Good. And next time, call me before you have three columns of things that are not yours.
I know. February taught me I should not wait until the end of the week to say I need another set of hands.
Mom we need to lock down the May 14 weekend. Are we doing dinner here Saturday or driving downtown for the Tigers game? Dad keeps saying 'whatever your mother wants' which is not an answer.
Saturday dinner is easier on the kids. Sixty-five sneaks up faster than I'd like.
Emma already volunteered to do the cake. Should I tell Aunt Linda to bring the apple kuchen Grandma used to make? Luke specifically requested 'the one with the crumb on top.'
Yes please. It's not a real birthday around here without it. Tell Linda the recipe card is in the green tin if she can't find Mom's.
Do you still want me to save the receipts from choir snacks? I can hand them to you tomorrow.
Yes, thank you. I am closing February tonight and the house numbers are landing around 5,642 before the church reimbursements.
That sounds like a kitchen table evening. I will bring the envelope and not add another errand to your list.
Appreciated. Don says I can leave the IRA page alone until after dinner, but I want it in the same folder.
Morning, Terri. Did packet 7 ever get the Psalm insert? I can trade you my copy before the warm-up.
I tucked it in last night but I'll check the stack. I also marked the lower women's line where it splits on page 3.
Good. And bless you for the coffee cakes. People move faster when they smell cinnamon.
I'll set them by the side door after I put the extra pencils back in the basket.
Did you feel it during Be Thou My Vision this morning? When the tenors came in on the second verse I had to sit down.
Yes. That's the one part of the week I never have to talk myself into. Standing in the loft with all four parts going, everything else quiets down.
Pastor Dale asked if we could do How Great Thou Art next Sunday with the descant. I told him yes if you'll take the alto line again.
Of course. Mark it down. I'll practice the harmony bit with the recording this week.
I put the anthem pages in your folder. Also, did Joyce find the red scraps she wanted?
Yes, she tucked them in my tote after Room B. I still have your alto notes on the piano.
Good. Save your hands this week; those tiny stitches before rehearsal looked fussy.
I put the alto folders back in order. Do you still have the blue hymnal with the penciled notes?
I will. Six chapters for the Tuesday ladies first, then I can finish the border.
Yes, and the penciled notes saved us last time. I also tucked lemon balm into the tea box for Marcy after her long week.
That is exactly the kind of thing she notices after everyone else has gone home.
I'll come early Wednesday and set the cups out before rehearsal.
I'm still thinking about what the woman from the Three Mile Square group said Thursday. The part about her son and the traffic stop.
Me too. I went back and finished that Isabel Wilkerson chapter Paul sent me last month, the one on the Northern cities. It hits different after sitting in that room.
You always come at these things through a book first. I should ask the library if they still have a copy of that Kendi one our choir director mentioned.
Sterling Heights branch had two when I checked. I put $40 on the Friends-of-the-Library account this week — they're rebuilding the parent shelf.
Found the old cooler in the garage. Still has the hotel tag from the Bar Harbor place.
Good. Keep it out, please. I put the island ferry schedule beside the atlas so we can compare the early boat with the afternoon one.
You printed both?
Only the schedules. I am waiting for the little automatic transfer on Friday before I print any deposit pages.
Did you ever finish that school packet for Friday, or is it still living on your kitchen table?
Kitchen table, of course. I have the salary page marked and the section about protected planning minutes flagged.
Mom would laugh at us with our highlighted paperwork. Dad kept every shop agreement in a coffee can.
That coffee can taught me plenty. I may grumble over the dues line, but I know what those pages save people from.
Mom did you see the Macomb clerk sent the August primary application already? Kind of early.
Yes it's sitting on the counter. I'm going to send it back this week so it's done.
You doing the permanent list thing or just for August?
Permanent list. Last November I spread the ballot out at the kitchen table for two nights and looked everything up. Standing in a booth I can't do that.
I found my notes from last Tuesday in the choir folder, of all places.
That sounds like me with all the underlined pages. I keep thinking about Anne waiting so patiently.
Carol asked if you would bring the Morrison copy next time. She wants the edition with your sticky tabs.
I'll set it by my purse before I forget.
Can you still help carry the choir folders Wednesday, or should I ask Marlene?
Ask Marlene for the big stack, please. My fingers are cranky by evening, but I can handle the attendance sheet.
Of course. And did you remember that little tablet before rehearsal last time?
Yes, Don put the bottle by my hymnal bag so I wouldn't forget. I also booked the March visit Dr. Patel wanted.
Did you still want me to bring the alto folder tomorrow, or did you leave yours in the choir room?
Bring yours just in case. I am outside giving the thyme and green beans a drink before I look for my folder.
That sounds like a better place to sort your thoughts than the church office closet.
It is. The street is finally still, and the hose gives me ten minutes before I answer anyone.
Did the Saturday room setup go all right? I found two boxes of donated paperbacks in the choir closet.
It went fine. I could have used those books for the cart there, but maybe save them for the library meeting.
I can bring them Sunday. Are you still drawing that little corner with shelves and a sign-up binder?
Yes, just a simple plan. Chairs, good light, and a place where people know what is being read next.
Service desk says the Equinox needs rear brakes sooner than I hoped.
Go ahead. I can pull from the cushion and we will do leftovers instead of Leo's Coney tonight.
Want me to use the rewards card there?
Yes, but only if we clear it with the rest of March statement like usual.
Finally hauled the last hutch box out of the basement. Your Hutzel certificate is in here, baptism papers from Trinity on Schoenherr, even Mom's report cards from Fitzgerald High.
Trinity on Schoenherr. I haven't set foot in that building in forty years. Is the cornerstone photo still in there?
Yes and there's more. Grandpa's naturalization papers from 1937, came in through Cleveland from a village south of Stuttgart. The clerk spelled the surname two different ways on the same page.
Mom always said her side was 'all English, mostly,' which never tracked. Dad would have a fit if he heard Grandpa Becker called anything but what he was.
Awake again. I wrote down the school forms, Ruth's music copies, and the insurance envelope so they stop spinning.
Leave the envelope by my keys. I can handle that one after coffee.
Thank you. I keep taking the whole pile back when people would actually take a piece.
Envelope is in the car. We can walk after supper if the sidewalk dries.
Do you want the car at noon, or can I keep it for the hardware store?
I need it by 12:20. Community Center bag is already by the back door.
The one with the rulers and pins?
That one. Then Marisol and I are swapping copies before she heads back to school.
Blue Cross statement came. Want it in the tax stack or the March stack?
March stack, please. I am matching it with the 10,500 gross line from last month's folder before I file anything.
I put it beside the Vanguard envelope. Nothing exciting in there.
Good. Exciting is expensive. I only need the plain numbers lined up.
Before you leave Kroger: please get the 9-inch foil pans, not the deep ones. Also check the turkey broth date.
I have the list you handed me.
I know. I added two things after Linda called and I don't want Sunday dinner turning into three separate store runs.
Got pans, broth, and the green beans. Heading home.
Do you want the blue tote from the garage before I put the car back in?
Yes please. It has the numbered binders and those napkins from Costco.
Same night you have to practice the part that starts under Ruth's?
Only that one page. If I can hear Ruth's top notes, mine will settle in.
I found the little notebook from the Tuesday stops. Do you still need the page with Dr. H's number?
Yes, please. I'm matching it to the forms I kept so the dates don't get mixed up again.
I'll send a photo after lunch. Carol said Shelby Township works better for her after 2 on Saturday.
Good. I'll text Megan once I know whether we're doing Saturday or Sunday.
You sounded wound tight on the phone. Did you go straight to the oven again?
Two trays are cooling. I only meant to make enough for Sunday, then the corners started disappearing.
Put the odd bits in a container for Don or toss them. Then shoes on and around the block.
The nice ones are going in the blue canister before Emma sees me with the spatula.
If I drop Luke at 4:15, will that mess up your late afternoon loop?
No, bring him. Don and I can go after dinner instead if the rain holds off.
He's got muddy sneakers in his backpack if you end up taking the short stretch by the water.
Good thinking. It's nice having that option so close when the kids need to burn off steam.
The filter is fixed now. If you type Kroger in that little search box, it should pull the grocery rows by itself.
I see it. March looks cleaner already, except the pharmacy one landed under household again.
That one comes from the bank name rule. You can drag it once and it should remember next time.
I wrote that on the sticky by the laptop so I do not ask you the same question Sunday.
I'm looking at the weekend of the 28th. If I drive in Friday after work, is Sunday dinner still on?
Yes. Megan is checking soccer times for Emma and Luke, so I won't know the exact meal time until she answers.
No rush. I can bring the laptop cable you asked about and stay through Sunday afternoon.
That works. Don will be glad to have both of you at the table if the timing lines up.
Did the article I forwarded last Sunday come through? The one Jamal from my team wrote up about referral data in Wyoming MI schools.

Read it twice. I brought a printout to our curriculum sub-committee Tuesday. Mrs. Okafor's mom said the same thing at the listening hall last week — the numbers match what families have been telling us for years.
Good. I keep telling you, the talking-heads on Channel 7 are not going to give you that. Your students' parents will.
I know, I know. Helen on our committee finally agreed to look at the office-referral numbers next to the classroom-library audit. Small step.
You sounded worn out after rehearsal last night. Was it the board video people kept sharing?
That, and the same old 2020 folders coming back in a new form. I put my phone away and copied Ben's small-group pages instead.
Bring them Sunday if you want quiet company after choir.
Thank you. I may. The pages are almost useful enough for other rooms now, if I can keep the language simple.
Choir folders are set for tonight. Are you coming straight from the building again?
Yes. I have to finish the seventh-grade paragraph scores online and tape tomorrow's sticky-note chart before I drive over.
I'll save your seat and a cup of tea. Do not grade in the parking lot.
I won't. The fourth-grade notebooks are staying in the tote until morning.
I put the folding chairs in the trunk. Do we need the blanket too?
For the gym, no. For next weekend downtown, yes if we're sitting in the shade.
I'll leave both. First pitch on the kitchen radio starts while you're making sandwiches.
Good. Then we can listen until Megan texts the kids' arrival time.
How did the meeting go yesterday? Did you actually tell them no on the spring fundraiser?
I said yes to one more. I know, I know. But if I drop all of it at once I'll be staring at the kitchen wall by July.
Ter. The kids in that classroom are going to be fine without you on every committee.
I baked three trays of broken cookies last night thinking about it. Don ate two and didn't say a word.
Late meeting again. Can you keep the kids until 6:15? Luke has spelling, Emma has the frog book.
Yes. I'll do spelling at the kitchen table and let Emma read the page with the pond picture. Chicken is already in the oven.
Please make Luke redo the sloppy words. He tries to rush you because you are nicer than I am.
I'll be kind, but he can write them cleanly. I'll send you the paper so you can see it.
I’ll get in Friday around 6. Don’t do a big production.
Nothing fancy. I have green beans from the freezer and tomatoes to use, and I’ll pull thyme before dark.
That sounds like exactly the big production you said you weren’t doing.
Then stop at Meijer for rolls on your way if you’re teasing me.
I can bring the choir binders by after rehearsal if that helps. Will anyone be there around 7?
Don and I should both be back by then. Megan's kids are only here from 3:30 to 5:15, and Paul is still on his side of the state.
I'll leave them by the side door if you two are out walking.
Thank you. The side door is easiest; Don put the spare key back in the kitchen drawer.
Ray called. Said the old gauge bench from your dad's line at the Sterling parts plant is finally getting cleared out. Asked if I want a couple of the micrometers.
Take them. Dad would want them used, not tossed.
Yeah. Funny — Ray remembered him from when Dad moved off the bench and started running the second shift crew. Said he ran a tight line.
He really did. Mom used to say she could set the dinner table to his shift bell. Grab the micrometers and the steel rule if it's still there.
I made the Google map layer you asked for. Stratford-upon-Avon is pinned, and I added Bath, Haworth, and Grasmere as separate colors.
Thank you. Can you make it so I can print one page for each color? The screen version makes me nervous when the Wi-Fi drops.
Yes. I will send PDFs. Please do not print until I fix the train times.
Still okay for me to come next weekend? Forecast says 48 and rain, which is peak driveway soup.
Fine, but I already have a folder tab waiting for the Shakespeare stop.
Come anyway. I grumbled through all that gray last month, but the wet pavement smell this morning made me weirdly happy.
I'll bring boots. Did you get outside today or are the essays winning?
Essays are ahead by a mile. I am trading the long loop for one lap around the block after lunch if the corners are not slick.
Mom, did you find my old robotics pin or did Dad toss that stuff during one of his garage cleanups?
Don never tossed it. Your box is with Megan's band folder and the Sterling Heights baseball photos.
That basement kept our whole childhood in cardboard.
It did. The oldest folder still has our first utility bill from 1985 tucked in front.
The church posted the Lenten supper sign-up on the Facebook page this morning — did it show up for you?
Yes, I saw it right when I got back from the grocery. Put us down for rolls and the broken-cookie tray.
Perfect. Pastor Dan also said the Saturday cleanup details would only go on the page, not the email blast, so keep an eye there.
Will do. That's where I catch everything anyway, the email folder I never check.
Heading to the hardware store. Anything?
No but can you swing by the church on the way back and grab my folder out of the choir room? I left it on the chair.
Same red binder?
Yes. The Old Rugged Cross sheet is paperclipped to the front, don't lose that one, I marked the alto line.
You sounded wound up after that committee call. Did you ever sit down?
Not yet. I am tying the zucchini row and pinching basil tops while dinner simmers.
Good. Call me after the sauce, not while you have string and scissors in your hand.
Deal. The yard is quiet now, so I am taking the long way through it.
Quick one and I promise I'm not making you my hotline. Aunt Carol emailed a chain thing saying the school flu clinic is using an old batch. True or eye-roll?
Eye-roll. The district posts the lot numbers on the parent portal. Luke's class did the same vial last Tuesday and he's fine.
Okay. I already checked the district page and the MDHHS notice, just wanted a human read. Thank you, nurse-who-is-not-on-call.
lol forwarded chains from Carol are 0-for-100, Mom. Always check the portal first.
Choir lunch is at 12:30 Friday. Carol is bringing those little party bottles again, but I can set aside tea for us.
Tea sounds right. Half a little glass is more than enough for me lately.
How is your shoulder after folders yesterday?
Sore but okay. I skipped the extra tablets and used the warm rice bag.
Do you need the car tomorrow night or can I take it for the oil change after dinner?
I need it. I'm going to Ruth's at 6:45 with the marked chapters.
The stack on the kitchen chair? One with the old cover and one with all the yellow tabs?
Yes. The Austen stays home, the Morrison one goes with me.
Did you decide on the school board race yet? You said you were torn.
Going with Reyes. She actually subbed in 3rd grade for two years and her answers at the candidate forum were the only ones that sounded like she's been inside a classroom.
Even though Karen wanted you to back the other one?
I told Karen straight up. School board is the one I dig into person by person. The big races I'll line up with the slate, but the local ones I read the candidates myself.
Did you finish your kitchen-table homework yet? You said you were going to look up the library board people.
Two of them so far. One has a Facebook page that's mostly her grandkids, the other I found minutes from the last meeting. Going to do the parks proposal tonight.
Ha. You're the only person I know who reads minutes.
Don teases me too. I'd rather sit with it at the table than try to figure it out at Beacon Tree under fluorescent lights with people behind me.
I can help you make that retirement sheet less ugly. What number actually hits checking each month?
Use $5,000 for the month. The top line is much higher, but the statement gets picked apart before it lands.
Got it. Separate tab for deductions? Pension, taxes, health, dues, that kind of thing?
Yes, and leave room for the salary-step notes. Those little columns matter when you are planning more than one year out.
You and Dad still planning the Toledo drive Saturday? Weather looks clean.
Yes, leaving 7ish. Reminds me - one of Brenda Whitaker's boys got stopped again last weekend. She came to me at conferences. I keep thinking about how your dad and I just get in the car and go.
That's been the conversation at every standup this month too. Two of the engineers on my team have stories like that going back to high school. It's not one bad night, Mom, it's the pattern.
I know. I'm learning that. Slowly. I didn't grow up around any of it - nobody in our family ever even sat in the back of a cruiser, you know that. So I'm taking it in from the people telling me.
The outlets in Auburn Hills are doing the spring thing this weekend. Want to drive over Saturday?
What are you looking for
I need a dress for Karen's June thing and a couple of work tops. You?
Nothing really. I'll come keep you company and grab a pretzel. My closet is full of things I already don't wear
Did you ever close that old campus-era Navient login? Mine keeps sending silly security emails.
I looked last year and it showed zero, so I just filed the final letter with Mom's paperwork habits in mind.
Good. Also, are you still coming Saturday or saving gas after the plumber?
Still coming. We covered that without touching the house draft or Equinox payment, just paused Joann's and restaurants.
Can you keep Emma for 45 minutes after school Friday, or is that your week with the tables and name tags?
Friday is clear. The tables and name tags are Saturday morning this time.
Good. Also Emma has three chapter books she outgrew. Do you want them for your library binder idea?
Yes, please. I am collecting titles that would work for mixed ages, not just the school crowd.
Sunday dinner still on? I can bring salad, but only if my chart review doesn't spill into the afternoon.
Still on. I talked to Linda earlier and she thinks noon is easier for everyone.
Did you ever send Mark the copies he wanted?
Mailed them this morning. Ohio should get them Friday, and I kept a second set with Mom's receipts.
Emma's history project — they have to interview a grandparent about 'a job in your family.' Can I send her your way Sunday?
Of course. Tell her to ask about Grandpa's plant and Great-Grandma at the school office, she'll get an earful.
She wants to know about Grandma typing report cards too. I told her Great-Grandma sat at the front desk at the elementary and did all the call-arounds when kids were absent.
And the report cards on the old typewriter, yes. She helped the secretary in the principal's office for years too. I'll dig out a photo.
Mom did you see the clip going around on X about the tornado outside Lansing? Wild footage.
I haven't, you know I don't go on that one. Or the short-video one the kids use. Send me the link if you want, I'll watch it on the browser.
Right, right. I'll text it directly. Same with TikTok, I keep forgetting you stick to the two.
Facebook tells me what the cousins are up to and Instagram shows me the kids and the garden ladies. That's enough screens for one woman.
Do you still want me to save two juice boxes from choir snacks for Saturday?
Yes, please. Emma likes apple and Luke will take anything if there's a straw.
I'll tuck them in the kitchen fridge. Are the little sheets going back on the beds again?
Not this Saturday, probably next month if Megan's work weekend lands the same way.
Do we need more butter while I'm at Kroger?
Yes, two pounds. The phone call with the insurance office went sideways and now I have dough chilling.
Two pounds. Want me to hide the tray scraps before the game?
Please. Leave the neat ones alone; Megan said the kids are coming by after dinner.
You sounded wrung out on the phone. Did Megan's form get sorted?
Mostly. Between that, two parent notes after 9, and report comments, I never made it past the front steps.
Tomorrow then. The thaw is making those front beds look alive again.
I know. I was cranky at the dirty snow pile yesterday, then stood there staring at one green shoot like it was a present.
Emma said you were at school late again. Please tell me it wasn't another meeting where people yell.
No yelling tonight. I stayed with Maria to sort tomorrow's groups, then found an old email from central asking whether I'd reconsider the full-time downtown role.
And?
Same answer. I can do a few afternoons on book lists someday, but not give up the morning mess and the actual children.
I can leave Grand Rapids Friday around 3, but traffic may push me closer to 6:30.
Then I will set dinner for 6:45 and keep the roast covered. Text me when you pass Lansing so I can start the potatoes.
Mom, that is a very exact potato trigger.
It keeps them from getting gummy. I also put clean towels in the blue room and saved you two containers of soup.
Are you still going to the opening market by Dodge Park this morning?
Yes, just for parsley if they have any and maybe a bundle of carrots. Kroger’s celery looked better yesterday.
Bring me two tomatoes if they aren’t hard as rocks.
I’ll check. If not, I have enough in the pantry for tomorrow’s pot.
Want me to set your phone so the score updates show on the lock screen before I head back?
That would help. Your dad keeps asking me to read the tiny numbers while we're fixing dinner.

Between Megan's practices and Paul's games, we spent half the 90s in parking lots.
Rough week here. Can I call tomorrow?
Any time. I'm at the 9:30 service then choir lunch but free after 1.
How do you do it every Sunday for 30+ years. I'd be exhausted.

For next weekend, should I grab that local cherry cider from Grand Rapids or just the Vernors you like?
Vernors, please. The cherry bottle would sit here until Labor Day.
Okay. Also I can bring the stronger back patches from Meijer if your hip is still nagging.
Bring the plain heat wraps if you see them. I am keeping the medicine cabinet simple this month.

Ancestry pushed an update. They finally split the Rhineland out from Swabia, and Dad's Yorkshire wedge ticked up to 28%. Mom you're now 41% North Sea coast, 33% Rhineland-Swabia, 19% Yorkshire, 6% western Ireland, 1% trace.
Don't tell your father. He's still bitter they took away his Scottish two updates ago.
Ha. Still zero south of the Pyrenees, zero Mediterranean, nothing from the Americas. Same tight little wedge through every refresh. The 1% trace is unassigned northern.
That lines up with what Linda found in Grandpa's papers last week. Send Aunt Linda the breakdown, she'll want to compare to her copy.
Mom did you ever finish that voter guide for the May ballot? I want to see how you're splitting it.
Mostly done. Health care millage yes. The expanded coverage proposal yes. Voting access changes yes. The library board I'm still reading up on.
Pretty consistent with where you usually end up.
I know. I'm not surprising anybody at this point. Don says he can predict 9 out of 10 of my picks. The tenth is always something on a city council seat where I split off.
Marlene at coffee hour was very worked up about a video saying the township is going to sell off part of the library parking to a developer. Have you heard?
I hadn't, but I went straight to the library board minutes from February. Nothing in there. I'll check the city council agenda too before I say anything back.
Bless you. You always read the actual paperwork.
Marlene's video was a clip from a different township in Ohio. Showed Don. He just sighed.
How'd the Tuesday meeting end up? You said Helen was being prickly about the swap.

Better than I expected. The Woodson book is in, one of the older units is out, and Marcus agreed to pull the referral counts for the next meeting. We also approved $125 from the building fund for the parent-shelf restock at the branch library.
Look at you, Terr. Mom would be tickled.
I keep thinking about the mom at the gathering on the 5th — her boy is in 7th grade. That stays with you longer than anything Channel 4 puts on at 6pm.
Pastor Dale asked if anyone wanted to help with the community supper at Trinity AME next month. I thought of you.
Yes, put my name down. I've been chewing on a lot of what families at school have told me this year and I want to be in rooms where I'm not the one doing most of the talking.
That's a good way to put it. Anything specific weighing?

A mom came to me about her son getting pulled over again. I keep realizing Don and I have lived a quiet life on that front, both of our families have, and I had no idea how different it looks from another seat.
Are you still free the Tuesday after Easter, or is that your Ruth night?
Ruth night. They moved us to the 21st so nobody is out during Holy Week.
Then let's do Wednesday. Are you still carrying that Morrison around?
Finished it, finally. Now Carol is pushing something new, and Ruth says Austen will come back before summer.
You sounded wiped out earlier. Did you at least get through those March responses?
Mostly. The online set is done, and I brought home one crate of spiral notebooks from the younger room.
One crate is better than three. Please tell me you are not going back in Saturday.
No Saturday. I am already at 45.75 after tomorrow's prep, so the rest can wait.
I can drive in Friday night if that still helps with the garage shelves.
Come if you want the visit, not just the shelves. I did save the old Tigers quilt for your room and made the herb butter you like.
The shelves are fine too. Send me the honest list so I bring the right brackets.
Three brackets, not four. I checked twice. And I printed Luke's robotics flyer for you to see at dinner.
I put the folding tote back in your trunk. Still need the poster board for the library stop?
Yes. The librarian liked the shelf sketch, but she wants it cleaner before I leave it with her.
After Saturday's coffee urn adventure, maybe label everything in big print.
Exactly. Big print, easy sign-up, and no one hunting for chairs at the last minute.
Did you find Mom's old property tax receipt? I have the folder but not the amount.

You and your files. Send me the number when you are sitting down.
I will after the 3:00 reminder. I want to check the bank bucket first so I do not give you the wrong thing.
Were you still at the center when I called? I figured the phone was under a pile of fabric.
Pretty much. Pat needed help matching corners, then Ruth texted about Sunday music.
You have more committees than I have houseplants. Did the six ladies like the ending this time?
Half did, half didn't. Marisol said the same thing at lunch yesterday.
I can pick up Emma after practice, so you do not need to add dinner for four unless you already bought it.
I only bought what Don and I planned. March should finish near 5,500 if the furnace behaves.
Good. Please do not redo the whole spreadsheet over one furnace noise.
I will try. I still want Paul to check the SSA login this weekend before I move anything extra.
Drove past the old Van Dyke parts plant on my way down. Half the lot's a Meijer now. Wild.

And Grandma made the sheet cake from the school office cookbook, ha. Whole block came. Half of Sterling worked at that plant or the stamping shop down the road.

Yes, please. I was counting copies, replaying my answer to Carol, and breathing too high in my chest.
I will take folders and refreshments. You take the tomatoes, the hymn sheet, and ten quiet minutes.
Thank you. I am trying to ask before it turns into another February Friday.

He says rest. I keep telling him I want a project. Maybe the literacy tutoring through the church. I don't want a Monday with nothing on it.
Are you doing your Friday morning lap before errands or should I call later?
Call after 11. Marilyn's group is meeting at the usual bench, and Don may join if he finishes the garage shelf.
You and that bench. At least you bought where you can get outside without making it a production.
Exactly. Some weeks that little stretch saves me from driving all over just to clear my head.
Do you still want me to save the article about the carriage museum up north, or is your folder already stuffed?
Save it. I have one sleeve for the island ideas and one for Maine, but there is room if I take out the duplicate motel pages.
Of course you have sleeves.
Laugh all you want. The England folder is worse, and I have not even printed Paul's train pages yet.
Mom, did Dr. Patel's office give you the portal printout or just the summary page?
Both. I put the shot record in the blue folder and moved the refill slip to my purse.

Yes, if the backyard is still muddy. I washed the twin sheets from the last time.

I asked for it. I also wrote down the two morning readings he wanted me to repeat next week.
Thanks. Tell Emma the pancake mix she picked is already in the pantry.

Use your old room. It mostly has Don's Tigers boxes and my sewing things now, so I just need one afternoon to clear it.
